summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with drainage and pain from a left knee incision following recent surgical interventions for prosthetic joint infection. Evaluation revealed no signs of active infection; findings were consistent with post-operative soft tissue edema and hematoma. She was managed conservatively with ice, compression, elevation, and pain control. Her acute kidney injury, likely due to volume depletion, improved with IV fluids and holding diuretics. Acidemia was corrected with sodium bicarbonate, and she was advised to discontinue sucralfate due to tacrolimus interaction. Her pain required an increase in oxycodone dose prior to discharge. She was discharged home with home health services, instructed to follow up with her transplant nephrologist, and to monitor for signs of worsening infection or complications.
